title: Espresso Spent Coﬀee Grounds as a  Dough-Restructuring Agent in Composite Short Doughs: Workability, Shape Stability and Baking Performance of Cookies
content: This study quantiﬁes how replacing wheat ﬂour with dried espresso spent coﬀee grounds (SCG; 0–20% of the dough mass), a by-product of coﬀee brewing, modiﬁes composite short doughs and cook-ies. The doughs were characterised by lubricated biaxial compression, spread-and-stickiness tests, oscillatory rheology and modulated diﬀerential scanning calorimetry (MDSC); the cookies by geom-etry, water status and colour. SCG increased the maximum biaxial extensional viscosity eleven-fold, decreased stickiness and shifted the thermal events of the sucrose–water, protein and starch domains. The consistency coeﬃcient of the storage modulus reached its maximum at 16% SCG and decreased at 20% SCG, which ﬂour dilution alone does not produce. A closed-form constitutive model, combin-ing a fractional viscoelastic element calibrated on the frequency sweeps with exponential strain hard-ening, reproduced the large-deformation curves of all doughs; the strain-hardening index was 1.64–1.89 up to 16% SCG and 1.21 at 20% SCG. The gravity number of the moulded piece (0.53–0.80) re-mained below the slump onset of a yield-stress cylinder (Y = 2). The footprint diameter of the cookies stayed within 3.3% of the control, and the restructuring of the dough was expressed as vertical de-velopment. Cookie thickness increased with the peak spreading force of the dough.
